research_question: Can k candidate outputs decide whether a new action should be added to an established benchmark-specific action library?

context_space.definition: every feasible current A7 subset S and candidate a not in S

split_protocol.screen: first k rows of each seed-specific held-out library-val block
split_protocol.established_heads: fit outside the library-val screening block
split_protocol.candidate_screen_head: five-fold nested OOF Ridge on only k candidate labels
split_protocol.investment_target: held-out test delta using the normal full-data candidate head
split_protocol.lowshot_target: held-out test delta after refitting the candidate head on only k labels

primary_decision_unit: one k-label screening block; split seeds are repeated trials, not an ensemble available to one decision
notes: The transferable object is the admission procedure; no action identity enters a decision rule.
Action value is conditional on the current library and is never treated as a context-free score.
The screen Oracle delta is an opportunity gate; the OOF Router delta tests whether the current information can realize that opportunity.
CoreBench and WISE have only 50 held-out library-val prompts, so k=50 is the largest strictly separated screen on those datasets.
The primary summary evaluates each seed-specific k-label screen separately. Averaging three screens is reported only as an explicit higher-cost ensemble diagnostic.
